t.1.97.1: Then Satyavatī, wretched and miserable, longing for a son, having performed the rites for her son together with her two daughters-in-law, O Bhārata,
t.1.97.2: Having carefully considered dharma, the lineage of her father's family and the lineage of her mother's family, the proud and illustrious lady spoke these words to Gāṅgeya.
t.1.97.3: In you are established the funeral offerings, the fame, and the lineage of Śaṃtanu, the glorious Kauravya ever devoted to dharma.
t.1.97.4: Just as reaching heaven is certain once a good deed has been done, and just as life is secure in truth, so is dharma secure in you.
t.1.97.6: I perceive in you steadfastness in dharma, the conduct proper to your family, and resourcefulness in times of hardship, like that of Śukra and Āṅgirasa.
t.1.97.5: You know the laws of dharma, O knower of dharma, both in brief and in full; you know the various sacred traditions, and you know the Vedas in their entirety.
t.1.97.7: Therefore, having placed my utmost trust in you, O best of those who uphold dharma, I shall appoint you to a task; having heard it, you ought to carry it out.
t.1.97.8: My son, your brother, valiant and very dear to you, went to heaven while still a boy, without a son, O bull among men.
t.1.97.9: These two queens of your brother, the lovely daughters of the king of Kāśi, endowed with beauty and youth, are desirous of sons, O Bhārata.
t.1.97.11: Be consecrated in the kingship and govern the Bhāratas; take a wife according to dharma, and do not let your forefathers sink down.
t.1.97.10: Beget offspring on those two for the continuation of our family; at my command, O illustrious one, you ought to perform this duty here.
t.1.97.12: Being thus addressed by his mother and by his friends, that righteous-souled scorcher of foes gave in reply words that were in accordance with dharma.
t.1.97.13: Without doubt, mother, you have declared the highest dharma; but you also know my supreme vow concerning offspring.
t.1.97.15: I would renounce the three worlds, or the sovereignty among the gods, or whatever might be greater than these two, but never in any way would I renounce truth.
t.1.97.14: You know what took place on your account for the sake of the bride-price. I, that same man, O Satyavatī, once again pledge my truth to you.
t.1.97.16: The earth might give up its scent, and the waters their own taste; light might likewise give up its form, and the wind might give up its quality of touch.
t.1.97.18: The slayer of Vṛtra might abandon his valor, and the King of Dharma might abandon dharma, but I could never in any way resolve to forsake the truth.
t.1.97.17: The sun might abandon its radiance, and fire likewise its heat; space might likewise give up sound, and the moon might give up the coolness of its rays.
t.1.97.19: Thus addressed by her son, who was rich in abundant wealth and splendor, the mother Satyavatī then spoke to Bhīṣma right afterward.
t.1.97.20: I know your supreme steadfastness in truth, O you whose prowess is truth. Should you wish it, you could create three other worlds by your own splendor.
t.1.97.22: Act in such a way, O scorcher of foes, that the thread of your lineage and your dharma may not perish, and that your friends may rejoice.
t.1.97.21: I know well that truthful vow which you spoke for my sake. Yet consider the law for times of distress, and bear the burden of your forefathers.
t.1.97.24: O queen, consider the laws of dharma; do not destroy us all. Falling away from truth is not praised among the laws of dharma for a kṣatriya.
t.1.97.25: So that the lineage of Śaṃtanu too may remain imperishable on earth, I shall declare to you, O queen, the eternal law of the kṣatriyas.
t.1.97.26: Having heard it, you should act upon it together with wise family priests skilled in the dharma and artha of times of distress, after also considering the ways of the world.
t.1.97.23: To her, lamenting thus, wretched and craving for grandsons, speaking what was departed from dharma, Bhīṣma again said this:
